body:
Should [19.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x24-V19-Config.md#security-verification-requirements) include something about how both sides need to be authenticated? E.g. if you are using TLS to connect to a DB but not verifying the certificate (e.g. self signed cert) then the encryption is a little ineffective.

I cannot think of the right terminology though...

comments.body:
1.  Verifying the authenticity of a certificate is definitely a must
2.  Whether a certificate is self-signed, signed by a local CA (which is by design self-signed) or signed by a public CA (which would be shipping with browsers or be part of the cURL ca-certificates bundle) has no effect whatsoever on the security of the connection (as long as you verify the certificate through other means than implicitly trusting the CA or anyone higher up in the certificate chain)
3.  Especially for the use case you brought up here, self-signed certificates are the way to go. Even more so if you're not only using this for internal purposes, but also use internal/reserved hostnames. (i.e.: You can't get a certificate from any reasonable CA for an internal/reserved hostname like *.localhost., *.invalid., *.example. and example.*.)
I committed something [here](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/commit/56f17df9c1e2b3db5a7e10c50ee7542c769bd961#diff-54f8ca1f5afa6981504509e08a293dbb). I didn't want to get too prescriptive.

title: 19.2 - include authentication?
